free_tier.stated: OpenVZ-512 at USD 3.49/month: 1 CPU, 512 MB RAM plus 512 MB vSwap, 20 GB SSD, 1 TB bandwidth, SolusVM panel, 1 IPv4 and 1 IPv6, in Los Angeles, Dallas, Mumbai/Pune, Paris or Quebec. The page states "Plans starting at $3.49/Month", with the same plan at USD 10.47 quarterly, USD 20.94 semi-annually and USD 41.88 annually. The tracker lists a cheaper row, OpenVZ_256 at USD 2.00/month billed yearly (1 Intel core shared, 256 MB RAM, 10 GB HDD, 256 GB/month, 0.1 Gbps, Los Angeles) and states "starting at $24.00 per year", but no 256 MB plan appears anywhere on the vendor page read, so this record leads with the plan the vendor actually sells.

egress.terms: bandwidth is a plan line item, 1 TB a month on OpenVZ-512, with no overage rate and no post-quota shaping policy published on the page read

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: root OpenVZ container with a SolusVM panel and TUN/TAP/PPP enabled, so any client runs inside it and no wrapper is needed; the vendor documents no API on the page read. OpenVZ is container virtualisation, not KVM, so the kernel is shared and a custom kernel module will not load.
chaining: At USD 41.88 a year this holds a public IPv4 with root and a SolusVM panel, which makes it a DNS secondary, a mail relay or a cron box; 512 MB of RAM and 20 GB of disk cannot hold a working set, and 1 TB a month moves control traffic only, so the data path belongs on a volume-quota host or an unmetered one.

limits.value: 1 TB a month on OpenVZ-512 is about 33 GB a day, and the 256 MB tracker row carries 256 GB a month, which is 8.5 GB a day.

notes: The tracker and the vendor disagree on the floor: the tracker sells an OpenVZ_256 row at USD 2.00 a month, and the vendor's own OpenVZ page says plans start at USD 3.49 and lists no 256 MB plan. A record that led with USD 2.00 would have quoted a plan nobody could order from the page read.
